sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时面临的一些重大生活变化、

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 转型，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode where we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身在世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，在这里我们剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today is a special episode because at the time I'm recording this and at the time you might be listening, it is Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 今天是一个特殊的节目，因为在我录制这期节目的时候，以及你可能正在收听的时候，恰逢情人节。

sentences.en: And each year on Valentine's Day, I like to pick an episode to do with how we can build and sustain healthy relationships,
sentences.zh: 每年情人节，我都喜欢挑选一个关于如何建立和维持健康关系的主题，

sentences.en: not just the romantic kind, of course, but our platonic ones as well, and how we can kind of apply psychology to better understand
sentences.zh: 当然不仅限于浪漫关系，还包括我们的友情，以及我们如何运用心理学来更好地理解

sentences.en: all the forms of love that we experience in this lifetime, specifically in our 20s, of course, but also some of the concepts and theories
sentences.zh: 我们在这一生中所体验到的所有形式的爱，当然特别是在我们二十岁的时候，还有一些概念和理论，

sentences.en: that we should have like a good understanding of before the decade is out to really set ourselves up for good, healthy love.
sentences.zh: 我们在十年结束前应该对它们有很好的理解，以便为美好、健康的爱奠定基础。

sentences.en: And in today's episode, we're going to do just that.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将探讨这个主题。

sentences.en: We're going to be discussing the idea of the mental load.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论“心理负担”的概念。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't be surprised if you hadn't already heard about this concept.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你之前没有听说过这个概念，我也不会感到意外。

sentences.en: This term, the mental load, has been doing its rounds on TikTok and Instagram recently.
sentences.zh: “心理负担”这个词最近在抖音和Instagram上广为流传。

sentences.en: It is the latest term that has become part of the psychobabble.
sentences.zh: 它是融入心理学圈子的最新术语。

sentences.en: But I really have my good friend Erin to thank for this episode.
sentences.zh: 但我真的要感谢我的好朋友Erin，才有这期节目。

sentences.en: If you are a long-time listener of the show, you will know that Erin, my best friend, is where I get a lot of my inspiration because she thinks about these things very deeply.
sentences.zh: 如果你是节目的老听众，你就会知道，我的闺蜜Erin是我很多灵感的来源，因为她对这些事情思考得很深。

sentences.en: She thinks about self-awareness.
sentences.zh: 她思考自我意识。

sentences.en: She's very self-aware, very thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 她非常有自我意识，也非常有思想。

sentences.en: She's always introducing me to so many new theories and ideas that I actually never came across when I was studying psychology.
sentences.zh: 她总是向我介绍许多我学心理学时从未接触过的新理论和新想法。

sentences.en: She's just like a book of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 她就像一本知识全书。

sentences.en: And last time I was visiting her, we got to discussing the idea of the mental load in our relationships because we are both in very committed, long-term relationships
sentences.zh: 上次我去拜访她时，我们讨论了恋爱关系中的心理负担这一概念，因为我们都身处非常稳定、长期的恋爱关系中，

sentences.en: with very lovely men.
sentences.zh: 对方都是非常可爱的男士。

sentences.en: And although we love our partners so deeply and they are such good people, we've chosen very well, there is a lot of invisible mental and emotional labor
sentences.zh: 尽管我们深爱着伴侣，他们也是极好的人，我们选得很好，但恋爱关系中确实有很多无形的心理和情感劳动，

sentences.en: that just happens to fall on women in relationships.
sentences.zh: 这些往往自然而然地落在了女性身上。

sentences.en: Even if you think that your partner is very much your equal, even if they are, there is such a hidden facet, a hidden component of love and effort
sentences.zh: 即使你认为你的伴侣在很大程度上与你平等，即使事实的确如此，维系关系的爱与付出中仍有这样一个隐藏的层面、隐藏的成分，

sentences.en: that sustains a relationship that women often take on.
sentences.zh: 而女性往往承担了这些。

sentences.en: So also known as cognitive labor, mental load specifically refers to the kind of extra energy and efforts women take on in order to organize
sentences.zh: 因此，也被称为认知劳动，心理负担具体指女性为了组织自己和伴侣的生活而承担的额外精力和努力，

sentences.en: the lives of themselves and their partners, specifically in hetero relationships.
sentences.zh: 特别是在异性恋关系中。

sentences.en: You know, the time taken to plan what we're having for dinner, when people's birthdays are, what we're doing on the weekend,
sentences.zh: 你知道，花时间规划晚餐吃什么、谁的生日是什么时候、周末我们要去哪里，

sentences.en: what we need to bring to the family gathering on Friday, the mental logistics of the week and of our lives, you know, the date night that's coming up
sentences.zh: 我们周五需要带什么去家庭聚会，一周以及我们生活的心理后勤，你知道的，即将到来的、

sentences.en: that we need to plan and organize.
sentences.zh: 我们需要规划和组织的约会之夜。

sentences.en: All of these small mental kind of gymnastics, all these small mental tasks that contribute to kind of the, I wouldn't say domestic burden,
sentences.zh: 所有这些微小的心理体操般的活动，所有这些微小的心理任务，它们构成了我不会说是家庭负担，

sentences.en: but the relational burden that each member of a partnership is kind of carrying.
sentences.zh: 而是合伙关系中每个人都在承受的关系负担。

sentences.en: For example, say that, you know, your partner's parents are coming into town next weekend, which means we have to make plans for dinner that night
sentences.zh: 举个例子，假设你伴侣的父母下周末要来这个城市，这意味着我们必须为他们到达的那天晚上安排晚餐计划，

sentences.en: that they come in, but they don't like Italian food.
sentences.zh: 但他们不喜欢意大利菜。

sentences.en: And it would have been a really long flight.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的飞行时间会非常长。

sentences.en: So we should make dinner at home, which means I'll need to go to the grocery store before then.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该在家做晚饭，这意味着我得在那之前去趟杂货店。

sentences.en: Oh, and I have to make sure the bed sheets are washed and pick up extra toothbrushes, but the bed sheets can't go in the dryer.
sentences.zh: 哦，我还得确保床单洗干净，并买一些备用牙刷，但床单不能放进烘干机里。

sentences.en: So I'll have to make sure that they're getting washed on a day that's really sunny.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须确保它们在一个阳光充足的日子里洗好。

sentences.en: That will have to be Friday, but we're out of laundry detergent.
sentences.zh: 那得是周五，但我们的洗衣液用完了。

sentences.en: So we'll pick that up as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也得去买那个。

sentences.en: It's this running to-do list of tasks
sentences.zh: 这是一张源源不断的任务待办清单，

sentences.en: that is honestly never ending.
sentences.zh: 老实说，它永远没有尽头。

sentences.en: And that I think sometimes men in relationships don't pick up on.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为恋爱中的男性有时并没有注意到这一点。

sentences.en: I think we are all very aware these days of the unequal division of labour in relationships, particularly in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在都非常清楚恋爱关系中劳动的分配不均，尤其是在过去。

sentences.en: How one partner, normally the woman, just seems to be instantly more responsible for household chores, even when they work the same amount of hours
sentences.zh: 为什么某一个伴侣（通常是女性）似乎瞬间对家务负有更多责任，即使她们和伴侣工作相同的时间，

sentences.en: as their partner or have other obligations.
sentences.zh: 或者还有其他责任。

sentences.en: How women are often more responsible for child-rearing activities, domestic duties, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 为什么女性往往对育儿活动、家务杂事等承担更多责任。

sentences.en: However, it goes a lot deeper than just performing the task.
sentences.zh: 然而，情况远比仅仅完成任务要深远得多。

sentences.en: Women also spend a lot more time thinking about what tasks have to be done, playing almost the role of like admin for the lives of themselves, their partners, their families,
sentences.zh: 女性还要花更多的时间思考有哪些任务必须完成，几乎扮演着自己、伴侣、家人，

sentences.en: even their friends.
sentences.zh: 甚至朋友的生活管理员的角色。

sentences.en: As one study published in the American Sociological Review describes it, women just spend more time anticipating needs, identifying options, making decisions,
sentences.zh: 正如发表在《美国社会学评论》上的一项研究所描述的那样，女性只是花了更多时间去预测需求、确定选项、做出决定，

sentences.en: and ensuring that what they asked someone to do is actually completed.
sentences.zh: 并确保她们要求别人做的事情真正完成了。

sentences.en: In my mind, we've all reached a point where we understand that men are expected to do more labour than their fathers or their grandfathers did.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我们都已经达成了一个共识，即人们期望男性承担比他们的父亲或祖父更多的劳动。

sentences.en: You know, we do split things 50-50, but that doesn't always fully take into account the added cognitive labour that goes into getting those things done.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们确实实行五五分工，但这并不总能完全考虑到完成这些事情所需的额外认知劳动。

sentences.en: You know, and I think a lot of times people just, partners, male partners in particular, sometimes need to be told what to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为很多时候人们——尤其是男性伴侣——有时需要别人告诉他们该做什么。

sentences.en: They may respond of like, oh, you know, you're upset that I didn't do the dishes.
sentences.zh: 他们的反应可能是，哦，你知道，你因为我没洗碗而不高兴。

sentences.en: Well, why didn't you just tell me?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你为什么不直接告诉我？

sentences.en: You know, I would have done it if you had asked.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你要求了，我就会去做了。

sentences.en: But the very act of needing to ask for help and expecting your partner to tell you everything that needs to be done means that you're kind of still treating
sentences.zh: 但正是这种需要请求帮助、并指望伴侣告诉你所有需要做的事情的行为，意味着你某种程度上仍然把

sentences.en: your girlfriend, your wife, your partner as kind of like the manager of the house, the manager of the chores, the manager of your lives.
sentences.zh: 你的女朋友、你的妻子、你的伴侣当作你家的经理、家务的经理、你们生活的经理。

sentences.en: It's kind of a lot like a workplace where obviously in a workplace, we have like, we have the employees and we have the boss and the boss is always going to be
sentences.zh: 这有点像职场，显然在职场中，我们有员工，也有老板，老板总是会

sentences.en: more responsible for what's going on.
sentences.zh: 对发生的事情承担更多责任。

sentences.en: And as an employee, you go back to your boss and you ask, oh, what needs to be done next?
sentences.zh: 作为一名员工，你会回到你的老板那里问，哦，接下来需要做什么？

sentences.en: What are some tasks that I should do?
sentences.zh: 有哪些任务是我应该做的？

sentences.en: But a relationship is not like a workplace.
sentences.zh: 但恋爱关系不是职场。

sentences.en: You know, no one is the boss.
sentences.zh: 没有人是老板。

sentences.en: No one is the employee.
sentences.zh: 没有人是员工。

sentences.en: Both people need to be truly invested in the outcome, in it together, looking for things that need to be done, looking for things that are going to make
sentences.zh: 双方都需要真正投入到结果中，齐心协力，寻找需要做的事情，寻找能让

sentences.en: the other person's life easier.
sentences.zh: 另一方生活更轻松的事情。

sentences.en: And I don't think that that is always what occurs.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这种情况总是会发生。

sentences.en: You know, we understand physical and domestic labour needs to be equal, but the mental burden remains very strong.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们理解体力劳动和家务劳动需要平等，但心理负担依然非常重。

sentences.en: And with that, the psychological burden of having to overlook certain things, suppress resentment, because he's still doing what you asked,
sentences.zh: 随之而来的还有心理上的负担，比如不得不忽视某些事情、压抑怨恨，因为他确实在做你要求的事，

sentences.en: but you kind of wish you didn't have to ask.
sentences.zh: 但你又有点希望自己不用去要求。

sentences.en: And also just having less mental space for other parts of your life and your identity and your interests.
sentences.zh: 而且这也导致你留给生活其他部分、自我认同和个人兴趣的心理空间变小了。

sentences.en: I personally believe this wears down a relationship in a lot of invisible ways, because maybe you can't quite articulate why you feel exhausted in your relationship
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，这在许多无形中消磨着一段感情，因为也许你无法确切表达为什么你在恋爱中感到筋疲力尽，

sentences.en: or why things feel unfair.
sentences.zh: 或者为什么事情感觉不公平。

sentences.en: You can't tell your partner why.
sentences.zh: 你无法向伴侣说明原因。

sentences.en: You just know you feel that way.
sentences.zh: 你只知道自己有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And I do think a lot of answers lie in this invisible cognitive and mental labour.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为很多答案都隐藏在这种无形的认知和心理劳动中。

sentences.en: Now, before we get into why exactly this occurs and the impact and some solutions,
sentences.zh: 现在，在我们深入探讨这究竟为什么会发生、产生的影响以及一些解决方案之前，

sentences.en: I do want to make a little bit of a disclaimer.
sentences.zh: 我想先做个小小的免责声明。

sentences.en: I think this is by no means a rant on how men are terrible and incompetent and idiotic and deliberately make women's lives miserable.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝不是在抱怨男性有多糟糕、无能、愚蠢，以及故意让女性的生活痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: I don't believe that.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: And I also know my boyfriend listens to the podcast and I'm sure he's probably thinking that if I was saying that, some of those statements aren't particularly fair.
sentences.zh: 我也知道我的男友会听这个播客，我确信如果我那样说，他可能会觉得其中一些说法并不十分公平。

sentences.en: I will say I'm very lucky that this does not describe
sentences.zh: 我要说的是我很幸运，这种情况并不符合

sentences.en: our partnership.
sentences.zh: 我们的伴侣关系。

sentences.en: My dad also was a stay-at-home dad and I saw him take on so much more of the mental and domestic load than my mum at times.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸也是个全职奶爸，有时我看到他承担的心理和家务负担比我妈妈还要多得多。

sentences.en: So I don't think that if we date men, if we know men, we are doomed to fail and kind of constantly be under the thumb of the mental load.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为如果我们和男人交往、如果我们了解男人，我们就注定会失败，并且会不断受到心理负担的压榨。

sentences.en: By no means, I don't think that.
sentences.zh: 绝不是这样，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: And I don't want this episode to kind of like find its way onto like the anti-feminist feeds on TikTok and have a bunch of people coming at me.
sentences.zh: 我也不希望这期节目落入抖音上那些反女性主义的动态里，引来一堆人来攻击我。

sentences.en: We are all about the science here and the psychology and the mental load is simply an identifiable and measurable relationship pattern and factor
sentences.zh: 我们在这里只谈科学和心理学，而心理学上的心理负担只是一种可识别、可衡量的关系模式和因素，

sentences.en: that I've become a lot more aware of recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近对它有了更多的认识。

sentences.en: And I think it really deserves some exploration and curiosity because in my opinion, it's definitely a subconscious reason why relationships struggle and fail and become unequal.
sentences.zh: 我认为它真的值得去探索和好奇，因为在我看来，这绝对是恋爱关系遭遇挫折、失败并变得不平等的潜意识原因。

sentences.en: We see a lot of people say, oh yeah, you know, my partner, my husband, he contributes so much, but I'm still so mentally exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我们看到很多人说，哦，是的，你知道，我的伴侣、我的丈夫，他付出了很多，但我还是感到精神极度疲惫。

sentences.en: I feel unappreciated, but I cannot articulate why.
sentences.zh: 我感到不被赏识，但我说不出为什么。

sentences.en: That is at the core of what we're talking about today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天讨论的核心。

sentences.en: You are describing the mental load.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的就是心理负担。

sentences.en: So let's quickly break down why exactly it occurs.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们快速剖析一下它到底为什么会发生。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about three reasons in particular.
sentences.zh: 我想具体谈谈三个原因。

sentences.en: The first one is socially conditioned gender roles.
sentences.zh: 第一个是社会塑造的性别角色。

sentences.en: The second is weaponized incompetence.
sentences.zh: 第二个是武器化的无能。

sentences.en: And thirdly, it's just like deliberate ignorance and disrespect.
sentences.zh: 第三个就像是刻意的无知和不尊重。

sentences.en: I think this is the harshest reason.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最严厉的原因。

sentences.en: And I would also say it's the least common, but it's still worthwhile to discuss.
sentences.zh: 我也想说这是最不常见的原因，但它仍然值得探讨。

sentences.en: I also want to talk about how the mental load applies to friendships as well, because I think that that is an aspect of this that our conversations around the mental load
